inheritedFindings.claim: The two count assertions are whole-file `includes` on lib/publicChatMessage.ts, so they do not actually pin the counts to PUBLIC_CHAT_MESSAGE_SELECT — any occurrence of the literal elsewhere in that file satisfies them.
inheritedFindings.reproduction: In lib/publicChatMessage.ts delete `memoryUsedCount: true` (line 28) from PUBLIC_CHAT_MESSAGE_SELECT and add anywhere else in the file a line such as `// historical: memoryUsedCount: true`, then run `node --conditions=react-server --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/memoryReleaseContracts.test.mjs`. Expected for a tight guard: failure, because the owner allowlist no longer selects the column. Actual: the test passes. Slicing the select literal out of the source (e.g. the text between `PUBLIC_CHAT_MESSAGE_SELECT = {` and the `artifacts:` key) before the `includes` would close this.
